title: Event 1
content:
Reflection on “AI Revolution & Open Claw” General Event Information Event Name: AWS VIETNAM COMMUNITY MEETUP AI REVOLUTION & OPEN CLAW
Date: July 25, 2026
Location: 7th Floor, Grand Terra Tower, 36 Cat Linh, Dong Da, Hanoi.
Organizer: AWS VIETNAM COMMUNITY First Cloud Journey team
Role: Attendee
Event Objectives Update knowledge of the latest AI trends on AWS. Introduce AI Agent and open-source AI applications. Share how to choose suitable AI Agent patterns. Explore how to turn AI into practical business value. Connect and exchange experiences with the AWS Vietnam community. Speakers Henry Duc Bui - Head of Engineering at CloudThinker Topic: Ship Fast with AI, Not by AI Nguyen Thu (Yuna) - AI Solutions and Business Specialist Topic: From AI Trends to Business Value - Sales Track Nam La - Cloud Engineer at Cloudino / AWS Vietnam User Group Admin Topic: AI Trends Through the Lens of an Infrastructure Engineer Tuan Vu - AWS Community Builder Topic: OpenClaw - The Rise and Practice of Open-Source AI Agents Key Highlights Current situation and limitations: GenAI and coding assistance tools significantly increase coding speed in the Inner Loop. However, bringing a product into production in the Outer Loop can still be limited by evaluation, testing, integration, and deployment steps. Solutions for the Outer Loop: The focus is not only on building more powerful AI models, but also on automating processes through lint rules, CI checks, skills, and documentation in the repository. Infrastructure trends: Cloud infrastructure management is gradually shifting from a reactive to a proactive approach through AIOps, FinOps, and proactive security. The future is moving toward infrastructure that can automatically manage and optimize itself with the support of AI Agents. Practical AI applications: AI is gradually becoming a support tool for many activities, including software development, system operations, data analysis, and infrastructure optimization. What I Learned Changing how AI-generated code is evaluated: Focus on design structure, how components communicate, and risks related to state, error handling, and security instead of only checking individual lines of code. Automating and preserving knowledge: Turn rules and common errors into documentation, lint rules, or skills that can be reused across different sessions. Strengthening testing: Use AI to help create test cases and testing tools for critical functions, thereby improving system reliability. The changing role of engineers: Engineers are increasingly shifting from directly operating systems to designing, controlling, and monitoring systems supported by AI. Applying the Knowledge to My Studies Organizing documentation in a repository: Learn how to build documentation and project rules directly in a repository to support both development and the use of AI Agents. Understanding the Inner Loop and Outer Loop: Clarify how AI can support the process from coding and testing to software integration and deployment. Learning about AIOps and FinOps: Explore how AI can be used to detect anomalies, monitor systems, and optimize costs when operating in the Cloud. Developing AI collaboration skills: Practice prompt engineering and context engineering, and learn about control mechanisms such as guardrails and rollback. Connecting with AWS knowledge: Broaden my perspective on cloud infrastructure, monitoring, cost optimization, and security through the practical content shared at the event. Event Experience A practical perspective: Approach AI from the infrastructure and software development perspectives instead of focusing only on AI models or data science. A clearer understanding of AI’s role: Recognize that AI should be used as a tool to support and extend engineers’ capabilities, rather than completely replacing human thinking and judgment. Exposure to new technology trends: Become familiar with concepts such as Agentic AI, AIOps, FinOps, and the trend toward building automated infrastructure. Learning direction: Gain a practical perspective for studying Cloud, Infrastructure, Software Development, and AI, while identifying the skills that need further development. Memorable message: “Ship fast with AI, not by it” emphasizes using AI as a tool to increase productivity, improve quality, and support system development. Lessons Learned AI is a support tool, not a replacement for critical thinking: Effective use of AI must be accompanied by human verification, evaluation, and decision-making. Focus on quality, not just speed: Faster code generation does not necessarily mean faster product completion. Testing, integration, deployment, and system quality must also be prioritized. Prioritize automating repetitive tasks: Rules, common errors, and review processes should be automated through lint rules, CI/CD, and documentation. Strengthen cloud infrastructure knowledge: Continue learning more deeply about monitoring, security, cost optimization, and automation to build a strong foundation for operating Cloud systems. Proactively learn about Agentic AI: As AI Agents become more involved in system development and operations, it is important to know how to build appropriate context, prompts, and control mechanisms. Develop system design and monitoring skills: In addition to hands-on skills, focus on analyzing architecture, identifying risks, and controlling system operations. Combine theory with practice: The topics shared at the event helped connect knowledge of AWS, Cloud, and Software Development with technology trends being applied in practice. Photos from the Event

title: Proposal
content:
AI Web Chat on AWS with EC2, RDS and Amazon Bedrock A cost-conscious and maintainable cloud architecture for an AI Web Chat 1. Executive Summary This proposal presents the architecture of an AI-integrated Web Chat deployed on Amazon Web Services. The system allows users to register, sign in, create conversations and interact with an AI assistant through a web interface.
The application Backend runs on Amazon EC2, providing a stable and flexible environment for the application runtime, libraries and business logic. EC2 connects to Amazon RDS, a relational database used to store users, conversations and messages with a structured data model. Amazon Bedrock provides access to foundation models without requiring the project to manage GPU infrastructure.
The frontend is hosted on Amazon S3 and distributed through Amazon CloudFront. Amazon API Gateway can be used as the public API layer in front of the Backend. Amazon CloudWatch monitors logs, metrics and operational issues across the system.
This hybrid architecture is appropriate for the project because it combines the control of EC2, the relational capabilities of RDS and managed AWS services for delivery, AI and monitoring.
2. Problem Statement Current challenges Backend runtime requirements: The application needs a predictable environment for its runtime, dependencies and API logic. Structured data management: Users, conversations and messages have clear relationships and benefit from transactions, constraints and SQL queries. AI integration: The system needs to send user prompts to an AI model while controlling token usage, response length and cost. Secure public access: The frontend must communicate with the Backend through protected HTTPS API endpoints. Operations and troubleshooting: Logs, metrics and database health must be visible during development and testing. Proposed solution The system uses a hybrid cloud architecture with four main processing flows:
Flow A - Frontend Distribution: The frontend is built as static assets, stored in Amazon S3 and distributed through Amazon CloudFront. Flow B - API and Backend Processing: The user sends an HTTPS request through Amazon API Gateway. The request is routed to the Backend running on Amazon EC2. Flow C - AI Chat Processing: The Backend validates the request, reads the required conversation context from RDS, calls Amazon Bedrock and stores the user message and AI response in RDS. Flow D - Data and Monitoring: Amazon RDS stores relational application data. CloudWatch collects logs and metrics from EC2, RDS, API Gateway and the application. Benefits Runtime control: EC2 allows the project to choose the operating system, runtime, libraries and application configuration. Data consistency: RDS supports relational schemas, transactions, foreign keys and clear conversation history queries. Flexible growth: EC2 can be resized or combined with Auto Scaling as request volume grows. RDS can be scaled and configured for Multi-AZ when required. Managed AI integration: Amazon Bedrock provides model access without deploying or maintaining GPU infrastructure. Operational visibility: CloudWatch provides logs and metrics for EC2, RDS, APIs and application errors. 3. Solution Architecture Overall architecture +-----------------+ | User | +--------+--------+ | v +-----------------+ | CloudFront | +--------+--------+ | v +-----------------+ | S3 | | Frontend | +-----------------+ API Request | v +-----------------+ | API Gateway | +--------+--------+ | v +-----------------+ | EC2 | | Backend | +----+-------+----+ | | +------------+ +------------+ v v +--------------+ +--------------+ | RDS | | Bedrock | | Users/Chats | | AI Model | | Messages | +--------------+ +--------------+ +-----------------+ | CloudWatch | | Logs / Metrics | +-----------------+ Main processing flows 1. Flow A - Frontend Distribution A1: The user opens the Web Chat in a browser. A2: CloudFront receives the request and distributes frontend assets. A3: The built frontend files are stored in Amazon S3. A4: CloudFront caches suitable content to improve load performance and reduce direct requests to S3. 2. Flow B - API and Backend Processing B1: The user performs an action such as signing in, creating a conversation, sending a message or loading history. B2: The frontend sends an HTTPS request to Amazon API Gateway. B3: API Gateway routes the request to the Backend running on EC2. B4: The Backend validates the request, applies business logic and communicates with RDS, Bedrock or other AWS services. 3. Flow C - AI Chat Processing C1: The user enters and submits a message. C2: API Gateway forwards the request to the EC2 Backend. C3: The Backend verifies the user and prepares a prompt with the required conversation context. C4: Amazon Bedrock processes the prompt using the selected foundation model. C5: The AI response is returned to the Backend. C6: The Backend stores the user message and AI response in RDS. C7: The response is returned through API Gateway and displayed in the Web Chat. 4. Flow D - Data and Monitoring D1: Amazon RDS stores users, conversations and messages in related tables. D2: The EC2 Backend writes logs while processing requests. D3: CloudWatch collects logs and metrics from EC2, RDS, API Gateway and the application. D4: CloudWatch is used to monitor EC2 CPU and memory, RDS connections, request counts, errors and application health. AWS services Amazon S3: Hosts the frontend and static assets. Amazon CloudFront: Distributes frontend content through a CDN. Amazon API Gateway: Provides public API endpoints and routes requests to the Backend. Amazon EC2: Runs the Backend and provides the application runtime environment. Amazon RDS: Provides a relational database for users, conversations and messages. Amazon Bedrock: Provides AI inference for the Web Chat. Amazon CloudWatch: Provides logging, monitoring and operational metrics. AWS IAM: Controls access between AWS services using the Least Privilege principle. 4. Technical Implementation Implementation phases Phase 1: Research and architecture design
Analyze Web Chat requirements and define core features. Design the AWS architecture and request flows. Select the required AWS services. Design the relational data model for Amazon RDS. Phase 2: Backend development on EC2
Create and configure an EC2 instance. Install the application runtime, libraries and Backend application. Configure Amazon RDS and its relational schema. Build user, conversation and message APIs. Configure the EC2 IAM role, Security Group and environment variables. Phase 3: AI integration
Request and configure access to Amazon Bedrock. Select a model based on requirements and budget. Integrate Bedrock with the EC2 Backend. Design prompts and handle AI responses. Store conversation history in RDS. Limit prompt and response length to control cost. Phase 4: Frontend and deployment
Complete the Web Chat interface and build the frontend. Upload static assets to S3 and configure CloudFront. Connect the frontend to API Gateway. Test sign-in, conversation creation and AI chat flows. Phase 5: Monitoring, testing and optimization
Configure CloudWatch Logs and metrics. Monitor EC2, RDS and API requests. Test API endpoints and the AI message flow. Test concurrent requests and database behavior. Review AWS usage and costs. Optimize EC2, RDS and Bedrock usage. Complete the internship report and technical documentation. Technical and security requirements Use an IAM Role for EC2 and avoid storing Access Keys in source code. Apply Least Privilege to EC2, RDS, Bedrock and monitoring permissions. Use Security Groups to restrict access to the application and database ports. Keep RDS private where possible and allow database access only from the Backend. Use HTTPS for communication between the client, API layer and Backend. Validate input and authenticate requests before executing business logic. Limit prompt size, response length and AI requests to control cost and abuse. Send application and infrastructure logs to CloudWatch. Store passwords securely using a suitable password-hashing mechanism. 5. Timeline +-----------------------------------------------------------------------+ | Phase 1: Research and architecture design | | Requirements, AWS architecture and relational RDS data model | +-----------------------------------------------------------------------+ | v +-----------------------------------------------------------------------+ | Phase 2: Backend on EC2 | | EC2, RDS, security configuration and User/Conversation/Message APIs | +-----------------------------------------------------------------------+ | v +-----------------------------------------------------------------------+ | Phase 3: AI integration | | Amazon Bedrock, prompt design and conversation history | +-----------------------------------------------------------------------+ | v +-----------------------------------------------------------------------+ | Phase 4: Frontend and deployment | | S3, CloudFront, API Gateway and end-to-end Web Chat testing | +-----------------------------------------------------------------------+ | v +-----------------------------------------------------------------------+ | Phase 5: Monitoring, testing and optimization | | CloudWatch, performance, cost control and final documentation | +-----------------------------------------------------------------------+ 6. Estimated Budget The project is intended for an internship prototype with low traffic. The final cost depends on the EC2 instance type, RDS database engine, storage, running time, CloudFront traffic and Bedrock token usage.
AWS service Estimated scope Expected cost Amazon EC2 Small instance for the Backend Depends on instance type and running time Amazon RDS Small database instance and test storage Depends on engine, instance and storage Amazon API Gateway Low API request volume Low usage-based cost Amazon S3 Frontend and static assets Low usage-based cost Amazon CloudFront Low traffic Low usage-based cost Amazon CloudWatch Logs and monitoring Depends on log volume and retention Amazon Bedrock AI inference Depends on model and token usage Cost control measures: choose small EC2 and RDS configurations, stop or delete unused resources, monitor running time and storage, limit Bedrock requests and tokens, review AWS Billing regularly and clean up test resources after each phase.
7. Risk Assessment Potential risk Impact Likelihood Mitigation Amazon Bedrock costs increase High Medium Limit requests and tokens; monitor billing EC2 overload or downtime Medium Low Use CloudWatch, health checks and restart procedures RDS schema is unsuitable Medium Medium Define entities, relationships and queries before implementation API or CORS errors Medium Medium Test API Gateway, CORS and request flows Excessive IAM permissions High Low Apply Least Privilege and review policies AI response is inappropriate Medium Medium Use prompt constraints and validate the application scope Project exceeds internship timeline High Medium Prioritize core features before enhancements AWS resources are not cleaned up Medium Medium Review Billing and clean up after each phase 8. Expected Results A working AI Web Chat that allows users to interact with an AI assistant. A Backend deployed on Amazon EC2 with APIs for users, conversations and messages. Relational application data stored in Amazon RDS. AI responses generated through Amazon Bedrock. Frontend hosted on Amazon S3 and distributed through Amazon CloudFront. CloudWatch monitoring for logs, metrics and operational issues. IAM, Security Groups and private database access applied to improve security. Practical experience with AWS Core Services, Networking, EC2, RDS, Monitoring and AI Services. Conclusion This proposal aims to build an AI-integrated Web Chat on AWS using a hybrid architecture. Amazon EC2 provides the Backend runtime, Amazon RDS manages relational data, and Amazon Bedrock provides AI capabilities. S3, CloudFront, API Gateway, CloudWatch and IAM complete the frontend delivery, API management, monitoring and security layers.
The architecture can be adjusted during implementation based on functional requirements, performance, resource usage and actual cost. The initial scope prioritizes a small, secure and testable prototype suitable for an internship project.

title: Self-Assessment
content:
Throughout my internship at Amazon Web Services Vietnam Co., Ltd. (AWS Vietnam), from July 25, 2026, to September 27, 2026, I had the opportunity to learn, practice, and apply the Cybersecurity knowledge acquired at the National University of Civil Engineering in a real-world environment.
During this internship, I fully participated in all meetups and completed a series of lessons and hands-on labs on AWS cloud infrastructure, including EC2, S3, IAM, VPC, RDS, Lambda, CloudWatch, Auto Scaling, CloudFormation, Docker/ECS, and CI/CD. Through these activities, I significantly strengthened my ability to configure systems securely, manage cloud resources, work effectively in teams, and write technical reports.
To provide a more objective view and accurately reflect my internship experience at AWS, I would like to conduct a self-assessment based on the following criteria:
No. Criteria Description Excellent Good Average 1 Professional knowledge and skills Understanding of AWS services, secure system setup, and the quality of hands-on lab work ☐ ✅ ☐ 2 Learning ability Speed of acquiring new knowledge about Cloud and technology tools ✅ ☐ ☐ 3 Initiative Independently researching documentation and completing assignments without reminders ☐ ✅ ☐ 4 Sense of responsibility Completing all tasks and worklogs within the required deadlines ✅ ☐ ☐ 5 Discipline Following the schedule for workshops and the program’s rules ✅ ☐ ☐ 6 Willingness to improve Accepting feedback from mentors to improve results ☐ ✅ ☐ 7 Communication Ability to discuss technical topics and present ideas clearly ☐ ✅ ☐ 8 Teamwork Working with, sharing materials with, and supporting other members of the study group ✅ ☐ ☐ 9 Professional conduct Showing respect toward mentors and fellow learners while maintaining a serious attitude ✅ ☐ ☐ 10 Problem-solving mindset Identifying configuration errors and finding solutions through troubleshooting ☐ ✅ ☐ 11 Contribution to the project/organization Level of contribution to and completion of the final capstone project objectives ☐ ✅ ☐ 12 Overall performance Overall evaluation of progress and development throughout the internship ☐ ✅ ☐ Personal Improvement Objectives Professional knowledge: Seek and learn more advanced knowledge related to servers, and further develop server troubleshooting skills.
Troubleshooting skills: Learn more about log analysis to resolve problems effectively.
Communication and presentation skills: Continue improving the ability to express ideas clearly and convey knowledge effectively to listeners.

content: Week 12 Objectives: Consolidate and apply the AWS knowledge gained throughout the internship to deploy an AI-powered Web Chat application. Design a suitable AWS-based system architecture for the project requirements. Deploy the Frontend using Amazon S3 and Amazon CloudFront for content delivery. Build the Backend API using Amazon API Gateway and AWS Lambda. Use Amazon DynamoDB to store user information, AI characters, and conversation history. Integrate Amazon Bedrock to implement the AI Virtual Friend functionality. Use Amazon CloudWatch to monitor system activity and performance. Optimize the system to reduce operating costs and improve response time. Successfully deployed the Frontend using Amazon S3 and CloudFront. Built the Backend API using API Gateway and AWS Lambda. Used DynamoDB to store user information and conversation history. Integrated Amazon Bedrock to implement the AI Virtual Friend functionality. Used CloudWatch to monitor system activities. Performed optimization to reduce operating costs and improve application performance.
